title: CBFC Clears Drishyam The Conclusion With Zero Cuts; 150-Minute Runtime Confirmed
excerpt: The CBFC passed the Ajay Devgn thriller with a U/A 16+ certificate on September 28 — no cuts, no modifications — setting up the 150-minute finale for its October 2 release.
body:
• The CBFC has passed Drishyam The Conclusion with a U/A 16+ certificate and zero cuts — no cuts, no audio or visual modifications, not even the usual disclaimer tickers or title-card changes.
  • The censor certificate, handed over on September 28, confirms a runtime of 150 minutes (2 hours 30 minutes) — eight minutes longer than Drishyam 2's 142 minutes.
  • It is only the second Drishyam film to get a U/A certificate with zero cuts, after Drishyam 2 (2022). The 2015 original ran 162 minutes.
  • The Ajay Devgn-starrer releases in theatres on October 2, the Gandhi Jayanti holiday, with advance bookings topping Rs 20 crore gross on opening day alone.

Clean chit, zero cuts

The Central Board of Film Certification has handed Drishyam The Conclusion a completely clean U/A 16+ certificate — not a single cut, and not even the audio or visual modifications the board routinely asks for. Bollywood Hungama exclusively reported the censor details: the Examining Committee asked for no changes at all, skipping even the usual requirements like mention of the title and credits in the film's language or an anti-drug ticker at the start and intermission.

The certificate was handed over to the makers on September 28, and its stated runtime locks the film at 150 minutes — 2 hours and 30 minutes, eight minutes longer than Drishyam 2 (2022). This makes it the second film in the franchise to clear censorship with a U/A certificate and zero cuts, and the franchise's second-longest film after the 162-minute original from 2015.

Context & Background

Drishyam The Conclusion, often referred to as Drishyam 3, is the final instalment of the Hindi crime-thriller franchise that began in 2015 and returned in 2022. It brings back Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar alongside Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat, Prakash Raj, Ishita Dutta and Mrunal Jadhav. Directed by Abhishek Pathak and produced by Panorama Studios with Star Studio18, it features an original script — a departure from the first two films, which were adapted from the Malayalam franchise.

Devgn has said the writing team worked on the screenplay for nearly two years, and the strength of the script is what convinced the makers to make this the concluding chapter. The film arrives in theatres on October 2, coinciding with Gandhi Jayanti — a prime national holiday slot.

Impact & Analysis

The zero-cut clearance matters for two reasons. First, it comes a week after the CBFC passed The Vvaan without a single cut too, suggesting the board's current Examining Committee is in a relatively lenient phase after years of criticism over arbitrary demands. Second, the timing — days before a Gandhi Jayanti release — removes the last uncertainty hanging over the film's opening. Advance bookings have been surging: the film crossed Rs 20 crore in gross opening-day advance sales with over 5 lakh tickets sold across more than 12,000 shows, and trade trackers estimate a Rs 40–50 crore opening day.

For a franchise built on meticulous planning — Vijay Salgaonkar's whole appeal is the man who thinks four steps ahead — a frictionless censorship process is a fitting start to the final chapter's rollout.

Diaspora Angle

The Drishyam franchise travels unusually well with the diaspora: its family-centred thriller formula works for Indian audiences abroad the way it works at home, and the Malayalam original's reputation gives NRIs in the Gulf and US a stake in both versions. The Conclusion will open overseas through Panorama Studios and Zee Studios, making the October 2 weekend a global event for the franchise's NRI fanbase.

What's Next

With certification done, the film heads into its opening weekend with trade expectations of Rs 40–50 crore on day one. The box office verdict — and whether Vijay Salgaonkar's last move lives up to two years of scripting — will be clear within days. The Videshi will track the numbers.
